meta.personalization: Centered on this project's defining recurring tension: the multi-session `/` synthetic-LCP saga (S147-S162), reframed in S162 as cold-TTFB/variance noise with RUM now live in R2. The honest resolution is to close the RUM->perf-budget loop rather than keep de-noising synthetic traces. Subtractive items prioritized per mature-codebase pattern (131 assets / 150 scripts). High-risk swaps are flag-gated. Obelisk-Phase-2 cascade (5 items) excluded as externally blocked, not audit candidates.

candidates.title: Close the RUM->perf-budget loop: make field p75 LCP the authoritative gate
candidates.why: This ends the LCP saga that has burned partial sessions since S147. S162 proved the synthetic `/` number is cold-TTFB and trace-variance, not a regression, and shipped live RUM to R2. The field data is the real signal — wiring it into check-perf-budget as the source of truth (synthetic demoted to advisory) is what finally lets `--strict` flip honestly. A self-hosted RUM feed driving a CI perf gate on a static GitHub Pages site is genuinely rare; most teams either trust synthetic Lighthouse or buy a SaaS RUM. We already own both halves.
candidates.recipe: Add `scripts/pull-rum-summary.mjs` that reads the RUM R2 bucket (via the existing Cloudflare Worker `/v/rum` ingest path or a read endpoint) and writes `data/rum-summary.json` with per-route p75 LCP/CLS/INP over a rolling 7d window. Extend `scripts/check-perf-budget.mjs` with a `--source=rum` mode that prefers `data/rum-summary.json` when sample count >= N (e.g. 50), else falls back to synthetic with a `low-sample` advisory. Document the flip criteria in DECISIONS.

candidates.title: Graduate Trusted Types from report-only to enforce on one low-risk route (flag-gated)
candidates.why: S157 shipped TT report-only with a /v/tt-report KV ring; the soak data should now show whether any real violations fire. Flipping enforce on a single static, low-JS route (e.g. /privacy/ or /terms/) behind a Worker path predicate is the safe next rung — it proves the enforce path without sitewide blast radius. Per the flag-gate-high-risk-swaps pattern, this stays scoped and reversible until founder real-device verification.
candidates.recipe: First read the soak: confirm the tt: KV ring shows ~0 violations for the target route over the report-only window. Then in `cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js`, add a route allowlist that emits enforcing `Content-Security-Policy: require-trusted-types-for 'script'` (not -Report-Only) ONLY for that path. Keep report-only sitewide. Log the canary route + rollback in DECISIONS.

candidates.title: Fuse commit-map + feedback themes into a provable 'you asked -> this commit shipped it' trace
candidates.why: S162 shipped two halves that nobody has joined: `api/commit-map.json` (noise-filtered git log -> Forge Ledger) and theme bucketing on /feedback/insights/. Joining them turns the existing hand-curated 'you asked -> we shipped' page into an evidence-backed one: each addressed theme links to the actual commit(s) that closed it. No studio publicly shows commit-level provenance for user requests — it's the strongest possible trust signal and it's almost free because both data sources already build every session.
candidates.recipe: Add `scripts/build-feedback-provenance.mjs` that matches feedback theme keywords against commit subjects in `api/commit-map.json` (simple keyword/tag overlap, public-safe — no raw feedback text), emitting `api/feedback-provenance.json` of `{theme, commits:[{sha,subject,date}]}`. Render a 'shipped because you asked' strip on /feedback/ that links each resolved ask to its Forge Ledger commit. Wire the builder into `npm run build` + `build:check`.

candidates.title: Add --warm to measure-page-performance so synthetic traces report steady-state, not cold-bucket TTFB
candidates.why: Carried from S163 Now. Even with RUM as the authority (#1), synthetic traces stay useful for pre-deploy proof — but only if they stop conflating cold-cache origin TTFB with steady-state. Hitting each route twice and reporting the warm number de-noises the local/CI signal. Cheap, deterministic, and complements rather than competes with the RUM gate.
candidates.recipe: In `scripts/measure-page-performance.mjs`, add a `--warm` flag that navigates each route twice and records the second (warm-cache) measurement. Default off; document that CI/local proof should pass `--warm` while `--cold` remains available for TTFB diagnostics.

candidates.title: One-shot orphan-asset detector across 131 assets/*.js + 150 scripts/*.mjs
candidates.why: Subtraction compounds on a 163-session codebase — and this one has accumulated deprecated approaches (mobile-wordmark variants, superseded nav-brand logic) that the memory ledger already flags as dead. A detector that flags assets/scripts referenced by nothing (not in ambient bundle sources, not in any HTML, not imported by another script, not in package.json) lets us delete with confidence and keeps the surface honest as it grows.
candidates.recipe: Add `scripts/check-orphan-assets.mjs`: build a reference graph (grep all HTML for assets/, all scripts for import/require, the ambient bundle manifest, package.json scripts), then list assets/ and scripts/ files with zero inbound references. Run it, manually confirm each hit against git history, delete confirmed-dead files, and wire `--check` into build:check as report-only first.

candidates.title: Wire scan-npm-supply-chain into build:check (CANON-023)
candidates.why: CANON-023 requires an IOC scan after lockfile changes and before push/closeout, but it isn't yet a build gate here. Even with a minimal-dependency vanilla site, a compromised dev-dependency (Playwright, sharp, the build tooling) is the realistic attack surface. Making the scan a one-command advisory gate institutionalizes the canon instead of relying on remembering to run it.
candidates.recipe: Add an npm script `verify:supply-chain` that shells `node ../vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/scan-npm-supply-chain.mjs --json` (sibling-path-resolved, skips gracefully if studio-ops absent like other cross-repo calls), and add it to `build:check` as advisory. Log the baseline result.

candidates.title: Promote inline pre-paint journey-stage snippet into shared assets/lib/pre-paint-stage.js
candidates.why: Carried from S163 Now. The CLS-safe inline head snippet that applies journey stage synchronously (shipped S161 to kill returning-visitor layout shift) currently lives duplicated inline. Promoting it to a shared lib gives home + /vaultsparked/ CLS-safe adaptive personalization for free and removes a copy-paste drift risk on a load-bearing no-flash pattern.
candidates.recipe: Extract the inline `<html>`-stage script into `assets/lib/pre-paint-stage.js` exposed as a tiny IIFE that reads `vs_visit_count` / journey keys and stamps the stage attribute. Inline a one-line bootstrap that calls it (kept inline so it stays render-blocking-by-design). Apply to /vaultsparked/ as the second consumer.

candidates.title: Anonymous opt-in telemetry on ?nav=sheet so the default-swap decision is data-backed
candidates.why: The mobile bottom-sheet has been founder-gated behind a flag since S160, waiting on a single iPhone verification that keeps not happening. Rather than block on one device, instrument the flagged path: open rate, drag-close vs backdrop-close, mis-tap rate. Then the default-swap is a data decision, not a vibes decision — and the same RUM beacon already exists to carry it.
candidates.recipe: In `assets/nav-sheet.js`, when active, emit a privacy-minimized event (no IDs) through the existing RUM beacon endpoint for open/close/drag-close. Add a tiny `/api/nav-sheet-stats.json` builder reading the aggregate. Surface the rate in DECISIONS when N is meaningful so the founder swap is evidence-led.

candidates.title: Complete the feedback digest backend: server-side sentiment-trend + top-3 un-addressed asks
candidates.why: Carried from S163 Now. S162 shipped the client-side theme bucketing slice; the backend categorization cron is the other half. A studio-ops-owned, public-safe-gated cron that writes sentiment-trend + top-3 un-addressed asks into feedback_summaries turns ad-hoc reading into a standing loop. Pairs naturally with #3 (provenance) — one surface shows what's addressed, this shows what isn't yet.
candidates.recipe: Scaffold the cron contract in this repo (`docs/FEEDBACK_SENTIMENT_CRON_CONTRACT.md`) + a public-safe `/api/feedback-summary.json` reader, and the aggregate SQL view shape. Ship the website-side consumer now; the cron itself is studio-ops-owned (cross-repo, ship via Ark cargo per CANON-018).

candidates.title: Week-over-week field-LCP anomaly signal once RUM samples accumulate
candidates.why: Once #1 lands and the R2 bucket fills, a lightweight detector that flags any route whose field p75 jumps beyond a threshold week-over-week turns the perf gate from reactive to self-watching. This is the layer that would have caught the S160->S161 14.5s regression in the field instead of via a manual prod trace days later. Low blast radius — it only writes a signal.
candidates.recipe: Extend `scripts/pull-rum-summary.mjs` (from #1) to keep a rolling weekly snapshot and compute per-route deltas; write anomalies to a signal file the Forge Ledger / status surface can read. Gate on sample sufficiency to avoid noise. Ship after #1 has a week of data.

candidates.title: Expose the Forge Ledger as a subscribable JSON/RSS feed
candidates.why: S162's Forge Ledger (api/commit-map.json on /studio-pulse/) is a public build-cadence timeline that currently only lives on one page. Emitting it as a JSON Feed / RSS makes the studio's velocity subscribable — followers, the Hub, and AI crawlers can watch what the vault is forging without polling a page. Brand-on (the studio narrates itself) and nearly free since the data already builds.
candidates.recipe: Add `scripts/build-forge-feed.mjs` that transforms `api/commit-map.json` into `feed/forge-ledger.json` (JSON Feed 1.1) and optionally `feed/forge-ledger.xml` (RSS). Link from /studio-pulse/ and `.well-known/llms.txt`. Wire into `npm run build`.

candidates.title: Measure which of the 23 ambient bundle sources actually execute on the homepage
candidates.why: The ambient bundle is 23 sources / 130KB shipped to every page, but some modules (rank-orb, founder-presence-handle, nav-sheet) only do work under specific conditions. A coverage report of which sources actually run on a cold homepage load tells us what could be conditionally loaded vs always-bundled — the data-driven input to any future bundle split, without guessing.
candidates.recipe: Add `scripts/report-ambient-coverage.mjs` that instruments the bundle build to tag each source, then uses the existing Playwright harness to capture which tagged IIFEs execute on `/`. Emit `docs/AMBIENT_COVERAGE.md`. Report-only — informs, does not change loading yet.
